utterances.text: I think given the number of hours we have left obviously that's a given.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Okay. So who's our next witness -- sorry, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think in connection with that I think we all need some intimation of how close we are to the end because then we may have to make arrangements for the joint experts and when they might be coming to testify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think we already indicated you might even get them in April, but that prospect as been receding as April progresses.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So unless something unexpected happens I think you're looking at May for the joint experts.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is that reasonable, Mr. Ivetic?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I think so, but obviously if anything changes in the next couple of days we'll let everyone know if anything --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think if you were to anticipate a much earlier finish for your case, a significantly earlier finish, like sometime next week you should notify; but if it's later than that --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Right, there's no possibility --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: -- I don't now see the point in having joint experts here. So I think the position in relation to them will be clear by the middle of the week, but even now it looks like May. Mr. Visnjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, let me just say that if the -- if Mr. Ivetic's case finishes earlier we need at least five days to organize other witnesses. This is just by way of information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, your next witness, Mr. Ivetic?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think we had one procedural matter that we needed to go into private session for regarding an issue of a third party that Mr. Haider had advised me about that we should probably do in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Oh, you mean you wish to raise a matter in private session?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, I wish to raise a matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, very well.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Anything else you want to add, Mr. Ivetic?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this stage for the reasons that we stated in private session we are -- we have no further witnesses for today and would ask that -- that the matter -- that the proceedings be adjourned until our next court date, which I believe is Monday in the morning I believe it is scheduled, at which time we will have a witness available.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, if Mr. Kovacevic is not available, then the two witnesses following him I think are listed as 92 ter witnesses and there are at the moment no statements for either of them, so --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We're expecting to have them this evening is what I was promised, but we've been having -- like I said, we've tried to get the assistance of our in-house translator in Belgrade to assist with some of these to get draft translations for some of these so that the parties had the adequate notice with the 48 hours prior to the date of the testimony, and we've been trying to adhere to that and we'll do our best on our side to get those out to everyone on e-mail as soon as we get them back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And what about the availability of Simonovic, is he going to be here on Monday?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Just a moment, Simonovic, I think he might be. I don't know. He's -- he will be -- he's here, but I don't know whether -- yeah, I -- I don't know. That -- that is -- that was not a possibility that I had foreseen. I guess I ought to have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, you just need to keep every possibility in mind. Mr. Hannis, no doubt, feels even more uncomfortable at that prospect but it's not absolutely essential that the cross-examination follows the examination-in-chief immediately. In any event, as long as you have all the possibilities in mind, then that would re-assure us.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I will do my best, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Obviously in a moment we shall have no alternative but to adjourn; however, we underline, Mr. Ivetic, that next week was a week where we had planned lengthier sittings. We've not been able to adhere to the idea of alternate days as we were able to in a previous period because of the number of cases in the various courts and the demands of these other cases. So we have to make use of the time when we can find it, and therefore you should be conscious of the fact that there is extra time next week, there are only four witnesses listed. So we hope that anything you can do to ensure that the time will be usefully occupied will be done. We shall adjourn now until Monday at 9.00 in Court I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 14th day of April, 2008, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 5.17 p.m.,
